rv.q: Before I Forget is reverential and well-meaning but it can’t quite marshal the disparate resources at its disposal – including Sophie Woodward’s considered design, Katie Sfetkidis’s lush lighting and Andrew Niven’s richly detailed sound – into compelling drama.
The result is less a comedy show than a joyful act of collective care disguised as improv.
If you've got a problem, Julia Masli is more than ready to solve it in her weird, funny and emotionally touching solo show "ha ha ha ha ha ha ha."

cn.t: This delightfully odd, audience-driven solo show creates a unique, bespoke experience each night, though its improvisational format means results may vary widely from performance to performance.
